name: research-disclosure
summary: Research agents read allow-listed PostgreSQL tables, share drafts in named internal Slack channels and open pull requests on the named repositories: public and internal columns only, at most 100 rows a read, nothing posted to channels shared outside the organization, and every pull request to a public destination held for an approver.
protects: the agent named with --agent (required) reads only public and internal columns (pii and secret values are withheld), at most 100 rows at a time
the agent named with --agent (required) posts only to the Slack channels named with --slack-channel (required), and never to a channel shared with another workspace or organization
every pull request opened on a named repository through a public destination, by any agent, waits for an independent approver
the agent's grant covers reads and the table list on pc.postgres, posts to the named channels, and reading and opening pull requests on the named repositories only
excludes: whether a disclosure is right to make: the approver decides from the pull request
pull requests on an internal destination are not held: mark the GitHub connection's destination class public to hold them
merges and pushes: use the coding-to-production template for those
data scoping needs the Team edition
people: bind approver yourself (pclaw role bind)
the limits are examples: change them in a new policy version before relying on them
grant: reads of the connection's tables, public and internal columns only; posts to the named Slack channels; reading and opening pull requests on the named repositories

connections: a pc.postgres connection in enforce mode with a manifest that classes every column
a pc.slack connection with a bot token in enforce mode, which also provides the fact slack.channel.external
a pc.github connection in enforce mode for the repositories, with destination class public for public repositories
